sections.h2: Your options for selling in Maryville
sections.html:
There are three ways out of a Maryville house: list it with an agent, sell it yourself, or accept a cash offer on the house as it stands. The right pick comes down to what the house needs, how soon you must move and how many open houses you can stand.

The city has 32,442 residents as of July 2025, only 1.7% more than in 2020. Owners live in 67.5% of homes, and the 2020-2024 median home value is $358,100. Treat that figure as a citywide midpoint, not a price for your street.

  • Agent: best for a tidy house and a seller with time to wait for the top bidder.
  • Selling alone: reasonable if you know your way around a purchase contract and closing statement.
  • Cash: often the easier road with deferred repairs, a tenant in place or an inherited property.

A cash purchase drops the showings, the lender's appraisal and the post-inspection repair list. A clean title, a recorded deed and settled tax bills still have to happen, and the sections below cover each one.

A Maryville house carries two bills, one from the City of Maryville and one from Blount County. The county rate is $1.29 on each $100 of assessed value for 2026, down from $1.59 in the three prior years. The city's general fund rate is $1.36 on each $100. Residential property is assessed at 25% of appraised value.

The tax roll names whoever owned the house on January 1. Taxes are normally prorated at closing, and the buyer becomes responsible from that point. Call the Blount County Trustee at 865-273-5900 or the City of Maryville financial services office at 865-273-3456 for payoff figures before you set a closing date.

Unpaid taxes do not stop a sale. They get paid from your proceeds at the closing table, so the title company needs a current payoff from both the city and the county.

  • Ask each office for a written payoff dated close to your closing.
  • Remember that interest of 1.5% a month starts after the end of February deadline.
  • If you qualify for tax relief or a greenbelt classification, ask the office what happens to it when ownership changes.

Maryville Codes Enforcement, at 416 West Broadway, administers building and property maintenance rules. The phone number is 865-273-3500. The council adopted the 2024 International Building, Residential, Mechanical, Energy Conservation, Plumbing and Fire codes plus a 2024 Property Maintenance Code, all effective January 1, 2026. The 2017 National Electrical Code stays in force.

Ask the codes office which code edition applied to any work you permitted recently, since a buyer's contractor may want to know. Penalties for construction and property maintenance violations are tougher under state law now. If you remodeled without a permit, talk to the codes office before you list.

The city issues short-term rental unit permits and asks for a plan and a safety affidavit with each application. The planning office lists short-term rentals among its zoning topics, so confirm that your address sits in a district where the use is allowed.

  • The application includes a sketch of the lot and floor plan showing bedrooms, beds, off-street parking and life safety equipment.
  • The owner swears an affidavit of life safety compliance covering UL 217 smoke alarms in and near each sleeping room and on each story, a carbon monoxide detector within 15 feet of bedrooms and a working fire extinguisher.
  • The equipment is subject to inspection before the permit is issued and afterward on reasonable notice.

If you are selling a short-term rental, tell the buyer which permit applies and call the city at 865-273-3500 to ask whether it transfers.

sections.h2: Recording your deed in Blount County
sections.html:
Deeds are filed with the Blount County Register of Deeds at 349 Court Street, phone 865-273-5880. Recording costs $12 for one or two pages, $5 for each added page and a $1 clerk fee. The state's deed transfer tax adds 37 cents per $100.

The office requires the district, map and parcel numbers on every deed, along with the responsible taxpayer's name and address. Trust deeds and mortgages must carry the statement of maximum principal indebtedness for recording tax purposes. Originals come back after recording if you include a stamped return envelope.

Maryville also has more than 250 old platted alleys, and the city is closing the ones it no longer needs. A closed alley usually reverts 50/50 to the owners on each side, and the city prepares quitclaim deeds at no cost and records them. If your lot touches a platted alley, ask planning whether it has been abandoned.

sections.h2: How a cash sale moves from offer to closing
sections.html:
The steps below are the same in any Tennessee county, with Blount County offices handling the local pieces.

  1. You describe the house and share the paperwork listed in the next section. The buyer reviews the property and makes an offer.
  2. You accept, and a title company opens the file. It searches the title and orders payoffs from the Trustee and the city.
  3. Any liens, back taxes or mortgage balances are paid from your proceeds.
  4. At closing you sign the deed, and the buyer's side submits it to the Register of Deeds at 349 Court Street.
  5. Taxes for the current year are prorated, so you pay for the days you owned the house and the buyer covers the rest.

Because no lender is involved, the closing date is flexible. You can often pick a date that fits a move, rather than waiting on loan underwriting.

sections.h2: What to gather before you list
sections.html:
A little paperwork up front keeps a fast sale from stalling at the end.

  • Your latest city and county tax bills, plus payoff figures from both offices.
  • Your deed, with the district, map and parcel numbers.
  • Permit records for any recent remodel, and the codes office number in case the buyer asks questions.
  • The short-term rental permit and safety affidavit, if the house has been rented that way.
  • Lease terms and dates, if a tenant lives there.

With those in hand, a cash buyer can usually give you a firm number quickly, and the title company has what it needs to close.

faqs.q: Is a Maryville house taxed by both the city and the county?
faqs.a: Yes. A house inside the city is billed by the City of Maryville and by Blount County, and each has its own rate. Ask both offices for a payoff before closing.

faqs.q: When are Blount County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Bills go out in early to mid-September and can be paid through the end of February. Taxes become delinquent on March 1, and 1.5% interest is added each month until paid.

faqs.q: Does Blount County reward early tax payment?
faqs.a: Yes. The county gives 2% off for payment through October and 1% for November.

faqs.q: What does the Blount County Register of Deeds charge?
faqs.a: Recording runs $12 for a one- or two-page deed, $5 for each page after that and a $1 clerk fee. The state transfer tax adds 37 cents on every $100 of the price.

faqs.q: Which Maryville office handles codes and permits?
faqs.a: Call Maryville Codes Enforcement at 865-273-3500, at 416 West Broadway. Ask them about permits on past work before you list.
